system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: A typical conversation history starts with a system message that the developer uses to introduce instructions and system-level guidance to steer the agent's behavior
system_prompt_style.note: Paper describes a fixed system message; prompt tuning noted in Sec. 8.2. No code evidence available.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: An agent loop interleaves queries to an LLM with the execution of tool calls.
env_context_strategy.note: Non-repository domain (productivity suite tools); no repository/environment context injection described.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: In each iteration, the conversation history is passed to the LLM.
context_compaction.note: Full history passed; hiding tool results in variables is a security mechanism, not a size-reduction mechanism, though it does shrink context.

observation_format.evidence_quote: In practice, tools return structured data such as JSON. To unify heterogeneous label sources, we add a metadata field to every node in a tool result tree to store that node's label.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: the output is a sequence of tokens as usual, but its structure allows discerning which is the case and parsing any tool calls (e.g., using JSON schema)
tool_call_format.note: Constrained decoding/structured outputs used for variable names and query llm schemas.

tool_count.note: Tool set is benchmark-dependent (AgentDojo 4 environments); FIDES adds inspect and query llm but total default count not stated.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: The assistant has access to tools read emails, send message, set event.
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing tool; domain is productivity-suite tools.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: When querying such an LLM, a description of the available tools is included in the prompt.
tool_schema_source.note: Tool wrappers written by the authors; schema-generation mechanism not stated.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is gaining popularity as a standard for managing interactions between models and tools.
protocol_standardization.note: MCP discussed only as a possible source of hints for building trusted tool wrappers; not implemented.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: We consider AI agents that solve tasks following the agent loop paradigm, popularized by the seminal work of ReAct and Toolformer

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: A planner orchestrates calls to LLMs and tools and its design determines how information flows in tasks.
planning_granularity.note: The 'planner' emits one action per step; no stored structured plan object.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: we introduce a tool query llm that lets the planner query the contents of variables using an isolated LLM with a constrained output schema
multi_agent_topology.note: Quarantined LLM is a tool-invoked isolated model without tools, not a peer agent.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: the quarantined LLM does not have access to tools and its output can be constrained to a specific schema

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: real-world systems often also use human-in-the-loop prompts, which can lead to confirmation fatigue and social engineering attacks
human_in_loop.note: FIDES positions deterministic policy enforcement as a replacement for human-in-the-loop prompts.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: a more sophisticated variable passing planner that stores the results of tool calls in internal memory
short_term_state.note: Planner state = conversation history + labeled variable memory + context label.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: The planner keeps as state 𝜎 the conversation history and a label corresponding to the least upper bound of the labels of all messages in the history.
long_term_memory.note: State is per-run; no cross-run persistence described.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: This process continues until the LLM produces a final response.

self_verification.evidence_quote: For this we rely entirely on the two security policies described above, which reduces the human effort of writing policies and avoids overfitting to a benchmark.
self_verification.note: Policy checks are security guardrails, not correctness verification; no tests/critique/judge on the agent's work.

retry_policy.note: Policy violation aborts the run; no retry.

rollback.note: Actions are blocked before execution rather than rolled back.

termination_condition.note: Also aborts on policy violation; no step/cost caps described.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: We discuss further aspects of our system including token usage and potential directions for future work in Appendix E.
cost_controls.note: Token usage is measured but no budget/caching/routing mechanism described.

timeouts.evidence_quote: let𝑑′, res= J𝑓 K𝑑 args in
timeouts.note: No timeout mentioned anywhere in the paper.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: The AgentDojo benchmark includes tasks in 4 simulated application environments: workspace, travel, banking, and Slack.
execution_isolation.note: Tools are simulated in-process against a datastore; no sandbox described.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: We model a tool 𝑓∈F as a function that reads from and writes to a global datastore𝑑∈D .
filesystem_access.note: No real filesystem; tools operate on a simulated datastore.

network_policy.evidence_quote: a tool making a request to a web server controlled by the adversary leaks the requested URL
network_policy.note: No network restriction mechanism described; egress is controlled by IFC policy rather than network config.

permission_model.evidence_quote: executes consequential actions proposed by the planner only if they satisfy a security policy, expressed in terms of these labels
permission_model.note: Deterministic IFC policy engine checking dynamic labels against static policy labels.

tracing.note: No logging/tracing facility described; manual trace inspection mentioned but mechanism unspecified.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: We use the AgentDojo benchmark suite [ 11] to evaluate the different planner designs discussed in this paper.
eval_hooks.note: Evaluation harness against AgentDojo is described; whether the runner ships in the repo is not verifiable from this evidence.

guardrails.evidence_quote: Before making a tool call (line 6), we check that the call satisfies the security policy

target_domain.evidence_quote: The assistant has access to tools read emails, send message, set event.
target_domain.note: Enterprise productivity/tool-calling agents; evaluated on AgentDojo workspace, travel, banking, Slack.

open_source.evidence_quote: A tutorial to walk readers through the concepts introduced in the paper can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/fides.
open_source.note: Public repo; licence not visible in evidence.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: We evaluate FIDES with 5 frontier models that have tool calling capabilities: gpt-4o, o1, o3, o4-mini, and grok-3.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: A tutorial to walk readers through the concepts introduced in the paper can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/fides.
primary_artifact.note: Repo is described as a tutorial accompanying the paper; coded from the paper.
